instruction: Set up VLC for multi-window video watching: disable all single-instance restrictions (both the general option and the file manager one), and configure it to always resume playback where you left off without asking.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

I want to watch two or more videos in same time on VLC. I tried to run multiple instances of VLC. It worked but can't play videos on those new instances. When I play video it plays on first instance instead of new instance.
Is there any way to solve this problem?

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VLC Tools > Preferences, found the 'Playlist and Instances' section showing both single-instance checkboxes and the Continue playback dropdown, unchecked one-instance-from-file, and saved. All three target settings were visible in screenshot 2.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VLC Preferences dialog, find Playlist and Instances section, toggle multiple checkboxes, change dropdown values, and save.
metadata.task_rationale: Maximum hardening: chains three objectives all visible in the same VLC Preferences panel (screenshot 2 confirmed). Disabling both single-instance settings was the demonstrated task; adding continue-playback=2 requires the agent to also change the dropdown from 'Ask' to 'Yes'. All three settings in vlcrc after Save.

llm_judge_reasons: All three instruction sub-goals are covered: disabling 'Allow only one instance', disabling 'Use only one instance when started from file manager', and setting 'Continue playback' to Always (=2).
Getter correctly reads /home/user/.config/vlc/vlcrc and extracts all three required keys (one-instance, one-instance-when-started-from-file, continue-playback).
Getter properly handles commented vs uncommented lines with uncommented taking priority, which is correct for vlcrc format.
Metric checks all three values against correct expected values: 0 for both single-instance flags, 2 for continue-playback (Always).
Partial credit scoring (0.34 + 0.33 + 0.33 = 1.0) is logical and proportional for three equal sub-goals.
VLC config persists in vlcrc on disk; getter reads the file directly so postconfig state of VLC running/not-running does not affect correctness.
The metric does not use the expected parameter (values hardcoded), but the hardcoded values exactly match the instruction requirements, so this is functionally correct.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Metric could read expected values from the 'expected' parameter (e.g., expected.get('one_instance_expected', '0')) rather than hardcoding them, which would make the function more reusable, but this is not a correctness issue for the current task.
